output.sql: SELECT p.method, ROUND(AVG(p.paid_at - o.order_date), 2) AS avg_days_to_pay, COUNT(*) AS payments FROM marts.fct_payments p JOIN marts.fct_orders o ON o.order_id = p.order_id GROUP BY p.method ORDER BY avg_days_to_pay;
output.explanation:
This query gives the average number of days between the order date and the payment date for each payment method, rounded to 2 decimals. It links each payment to its order and also counts the payments per method.

Every payment counts, whatever the order's status, so I didn't filter on the revenue flag (is_revenue). If an order was paid in more than one payment, each payment counts separately. Results are sorted from the fastest-paying method to the slowest.
